record.paper_title: Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology
record.original_question: Let X be an arbitrary paracompact p-space, meaning a preimage of a metrizable space under a perfect mapping. Is the free topological group F(X) on X necessarily paracompact?

evidence.quote:
Problem 10 (A. V. Arhangel’skii, 1981) . Is the free topological group F (X) of an
arbitrary paracompact p-space X paracompact?

We remind that a paracompact p-space is a preimage of a metrizable space under a
perfect mapping [4].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that a Tychonoff space $X$ is called a paracompact $p$-space if it is the preimage of a metrizable space under a perfect (continuous, closed, surjective with compact fibers) mapping. For a Tychonoff space $X$, let $F(X)$ denote the (Markov) free topological group on $X$: the unique (up to topological isomorphism) Hausdorff topological group containing $X$ as a closed topological subspace that algebraically generates it freely, characterized by the universal property that every continuous map from $X$ into a Hausdorff topological group $G$ extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism $F(X) \to G$.

Question: Is it true that for every paracompact $p$-space $X$, the free topological group $F(X)$ is paracompact?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, posed by A. V. Arhangel'skii in 1981, is still listed as an open problem in surveys on topological algebra. The metrizable case is known to be affirmative, but the general paracompact p-space case remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A note on some open problems in topological algebra
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 0.5: Suppose that X is a paracompact p-space. Then is its free topological group F(X) paracompact? Affirmative for metrizable X (Arhangelskii 1981).
status_evidence.claim: Problem listed as open in a survey of open problems in topological algebra.
